paragraphs: Mango Languages sells language courses covering more than 70 languages and dialects, plus English for speakers of more than 20 others. Individuals subscribe, and the company also offers custom arrangements for organizations of any size.

Rather than separating vocabulary, grammar and listening into their own exercises, every lesson works all of them at once inside a real conversation. Each lesson asks the learner to say the phrase out loud before moving on, then plays the recording back against a native speaker. The courses are taught through thousands of authentic native-speaker recordings rather than synthetic voice.

Many public libraries and schools give their patrons full access at no cost, with nothing more than a library card. The school version is pitched as getting students speaking from day one while giving a district the reporting it needs. Mango launched in August 2007, paid for by a web development company two brothers had built in Detroit. It is still led by the four people who started it.
